public_rationale: The linked paper, dated February 20, 2026, identifies six vulnerability classes as unique to autonomous agents or significantly amplified compared with stateless LLMs [e1]. Its taxonomy explains mechanisms involving persistent memory, tool use, multistep actions and delegation [e1]. This supports the claim's qualitative description of the paper's taxonomy [e1].
limitations: The taxonomy does not establish numerical differences in vulnerability against matched stateless-LLM controls.
The supplied evidence does not establish independent replication of the paper's empirical findings.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: The new study of autonomous agent deployments shows that agents are in many ways much more vulnerable than pure (stateless) LLMs, as set out in the taxonomy its authors developed.
conditions: as shown by the new paper's taxonomy

statement.excerpt: Importantly the new paper shows that agents are in many ways much more vulnerable than pure (“stateless”) LLMs, as discussed in a taxonomy they developed:
statement.document_title: Breaking: Autonomous Agents are a Shitshow

from_speaker: in many ways much more vulnerable
as discussed in a taxonomy they developed
our_interpretation: The plain reading is that the cited paper identifies several substantial additional or amplified vulnerabilities in autonomous agents compared with stateless LLMs.
The reference to a taxonomy makes this a qualitative comparison of attack surfaces and vulnerability classes. Marcus supplies no numerical comparative threshold.
The target is the cited paper available before the post on 2026-05-05. No beginning date is specified; this is an observation about a publication, not a reporting-period statistic.
criteria.support_condition: The cited paper's taxonomy identifies multiple vulnerability classes as unique to autonomous agents or substantially amplified relative to stateless LLMs, with explanations of the architectural differences.
criteria.contradiction_condition: The cited paper rejects that comparison, finds comparable or lower vulnerability across the relevant classes, or its taxonomy does not identify multiple additional or substantially amplified vulnerabilities.
